purpose: The declared internal-operations flow estate: every endpoint contract key, the physical Power Automate flow behind it, its workflow id where the corpus records one, and the definition file in this repository that covers it. scripts/flow-list-sweep.mjs reads this to state contract coverage; it never infers an attribution from a filename.
whyItMatters: The full-scope provisioning gate is held open by "Internal operations — 7 of ~20 flow definitions available". That count is of CONTRACT KEYS. Several keys share one physical flow, so the number of flows that actually have to be exported is smaller than the number of keys — this register is where that arithmetic is visible rather than assumed.
credentialPolicy: Workflow ids only. A signed trigger URL is a bearer credential and its sig token is never recorded here, in line with scripts/flow-inventory.mjs.

IP_FETCH_ALL_ENDPOINT was exported on 2026-09-03 and compared against docs/deployment/internal/flows/designer-paste/DGO_FETCH_ALL.designer-paste.json by scripts/compare-live-export.mjs: 0 actions missing, 0 different, 0 extra, the paste container deleted and the trigger Method = POST. The id is the definition's own `name` / `id` — /providers/Microsoft.Flow/flows/b79e6707-df4d-4ae7-8a65-738aa45e9a73 — dashless, which is the form a trigger URL carries. NOT the export's folder name: a legacy package stores each flow under a directory that Microsoft.Flow/flows/manifest.json calls an assetPath, and for this export that path is 6e810636-aaab-4180-bbd7-dd6b9e134a6f, which is not the flow and appears nowhere in the tenant. The distinction is corroborated by a second export read the same day: Single_Task_Assignment sits under assetPath 493d5a51-1429-4ca4-adf1-7f25c26e57e6 while its definition declares 3caf9458-8d95-4740-a01b-6803dad97d34, and the operator's own reading of that flow in Power Automate gave the definition's value. The three deployed definitions below belong to the flow FETCH_ALL pointed at BEFORE the rebuild and are kept for their list footprint, which is what the coverage gate reads them for. TWO DIFFERENT IDENTIFIERS, AND THIS FIELD IS THE OTHER ONE. A Power Automate flow carries a flow id — the GUID in make.powerautomate.com/…/flows/<id>/details, in a legacy export's definition `name` / `id` (/providers/Microsoft.Flow/flows/<id>), and in the maker portal's Flow identifier. Its trigger URL carries a DIFFERENT id in /workflows/<id>/triggers/manual/paths/invoke. This register records the second: every settled entry here is sourced from a labelled trigger URL or from a definition's own workflow_identity, and scripts/check-config-local.mjs compares a config.local.js against it by pulling that id out of the URL. EMAIL_RELATED_TASK proves the pairing — a942d230337c4ddfa9a386e92bbd048b, recorded from workflow_identity, matches the operator's live URL exactly. The value below was read from an export's definition `name`, which is the flow id, so it is the wrong class for this field and is preserved as flowId rather than asserted as the workflow id. The trigger URL of the correctly-named flow is the only source for the right one. Values previously held in this field: 31e02518075940d2bcfa9bdb0e9b0b8d / 4a250f97181b4a28abc1d0fb0f7d4c4d. RESOLVED 2026-09-04 FROM A TENANT NAME-TO-WORKFLOW-ID MAP supplied by the operator, which lists each flow by display name against the id its trigger URL carries — the identifier this field holds, not the flow id. That was wrong twice over: the definition was a POST tenant-authenticated Portal Registry feed that reads no X-DGO-* header, and the file itself carried a workflow id belonging to a different flow. It was emptied on 2026-09-03 when the key was genuinely unbuilt, and carries a real definition for the first time on 2026-09-04.

changelog.what: Attributed every physical flow to a definition exported from the live tenant on 2026-08-19. All 16 flows and all 20 contract keys are now covered by a deployed definition rather than by a capture, an inference or nothing. Where more than one deployed flow carries the right shape, every candidate is attributed so the footprint is a union rather than a guess, and the note says whether the ambiguity can affect the gate.

Read workflow_identity out of the definitions themselves. That confirmed REFERENCE_DATA and DYNAMIC_GLOBAL_ACTIONS, settled the EMAIL_RELATED_TASK conflict, supplied both OTP ids that no labelled register held, and opened a new conflict on BULK_ASSIGNMENT. Two definitions were also recovered from deleted git history: Dynamic_Multi-Actions (closes four contract keys) and a copy of the fetch-all flow.

Consolidation of the five most recently updated branches. SCAN_INTAKE takes the claude/system-remediation-gaps-ahpmsy row (IP_SCAN_INTAKE 5504d7f9-cc96-470c-be79-217582faf415, tenant export attached, checked by npm run test:keyimpl); the superseded ECM_DOCS_INTAKE attribution is not restored. Every other key keeps the claude/fetchall-flow-error-1h94u5 tenant-sourced ids. The OTP rows keep the claude/sharepoint-lists-gap-bqo7j7 two-flow model, so physicalFlows returns to 16.
